faq.a: Janaat is associated with the Arabic form جنات, whose core sense is gardens; gardens of paradise.

faq.q: What is the origin of Janaat?
faq.a: Janaat is associated with Arabic. Janaat is Arabic جَنَّات (Jannāt) 'gardens; gardens of paradise', the plural of جَنَّة (janna). The source gloss 'Garden of Paradise' is broadly consistent. Same name as janat and jannat.
Yes — the underlying form جنات is Arabic.

faq.q: What does Janaat mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Janaat is rendered جنات and carries the sense جنات، باغها، بهشت.
A romanized syllable approximation is ja-naat. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Janaat?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Janaat, janaat, janat. Script forms are جنات, जन्नात.

faq.q: Is Janaat a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
